In order to protect students from sexual harassment at the institutional level, the Government has issued protective guidelines on “students’ safety and protection from sexual violence”. A “Student Safety Advisory Committee” has to be set up in each school to monitor

21

students safety and wellbeing. A control room will be set up at DPI with a toll free hotline and private email facility to receive complaints specifically pertaining to sexual harassment and violence at schools, from students, parents and others.

ORDER:-

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 has been enacted by the Government of India to protect the Rights of the Persons with Disabilities. Section 21 of the said Act provides as follows:-

Section 21 of the Act:-

“(1) Every establishment shall notify equal opportunity policy detailing measures proposed to be taken by it in pursuance of the provisions of this Chapter in the manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government.

(2) Every establishment shall register a copy of the said policy with the Chief Commissioner or the State Commissioner, as the case may be”.

In section 2 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, establishment defined as follows:-

2(i) “establishment” includes a Government establishment and private establishment;

2(k) “Government establishment” means a corporation established by or under a Central Act or State Act or an authority or a body owned or controlled or aided by the Government or a local authority or a Government company as defined in section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013) and includes a Department of the Government,

2

2(v) “private establishment” means a company, firm, cooperative or other society, associations, trust, agency, institution, organisation, union, factory or such other establishment as the appropriate Government may, by notification, specify;

2. Accordingly, the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017 has been framed by the Government of India. Rules 8 and 9 of the aforesaid rules provides as follows:-

Rule 8 - Manner of publication of equal opportunity policy.-

(1) Every establishment shall publish equal opportunity policy for persons with disabilities.

(2) The establishment shall display the equal opportunity policy preferably on their website, failing which at conspicuous places in their premises.

e Ground water recharge.

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for the Implementation of Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam (KNMT)

1. Introduction

In Tamil Nadu, there are 14 Corporations (except Greater Chennai Corporation), 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats. Many schemes taken up in the recent years such as Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT are aimed at improving the infrastructure facilities of Corporations and major towns alone. Smart Cities Mission is being implemented only in 11 Corporations. AMRUT is also being implemented in 28 Towns only. The coverage of schemes in Corporations is relatively high when compared to Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Hence it has been decided to introduce a new Scheme “Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam”’(KNMT) in all 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats so as to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in these Urban Local

Bodies. 2. Implementation Plan

The vision of the Government is providing water service connection to all urban house holds, safe sewer disposal to each household either through UGSS or through FSTP, street lights and good road facilities. Though there are schemes for the provision of 100% functional household tap connections, sewer links, roads, such are highly capital intensive, mostly covering only prominent areas in the Urban Local Bodies. Infrastructure gaps remain existing in many backward areas/ slums and also newly added areas of the Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Considering the above factors, it has been decided to give preference to the slum areas/ backward areas and added areas of the ULBs for the implementation of KNMT.

2.1 Urban Development Plan (UDP)

The distribution of basic amenities is not uniform across the Urban Local Bodies and in certain wards / specific areas, the basic amenities are still inadequate. In order to have an equitable distribution of basic amenities, a detailed survey will be conducted and an Urban Development Plan (UDP) will be prepared for each urban local body so as to assess the present availability of basic infrastructure and the gaps

to be fulfilled.

The detailed survey will be conducted ward wise, with respect to the availability of water supply, sanitation, internal roads, street lights,

burial ground / crematorium availability and other community infrastructure. With regard to roads, a detailed Roads Network Plan will be prepared indicating all the major roads maintained by various agencies viz National Highways, State Highways and Municipalities / Town Panchayats (Access roads and internal streets) in the Urban Local Bodies concerned. With respect to water supply, the total demand, including the present supply and the future requirement will be taken into account and incorporated. Based on this, a “City Water balance Plan” will be prepared for each Urban Local Body. Similar survey and assessment of the gaps will be undertaken for all needed components of the ULBs concerned.

In Agriculture, after harvest, nearly 10 % of the produce are lost as Post Harvest Losses either by Biotic factors like insects, rodents, fungi and bacteria or by abiotic factors such as moisture, humidity, temperature etc., Post Harvest Losses are a major area of concern since agricultural production is seasonal while the demands for agricultural commodities are more evenly spread throughout the year.

Further, at many times, it has been noticed that during the peak harvest the quantum of paddy arrivals to Direct Purchase Centres are high and due to less protected storage facilities the lots are damaged due to unpredicted rains, wind, etc.,

In order to satisfy the demand for a plentiful supply, grains must be stored throughout the year. A substantial amount of food grains is being damaged after harvest due to lack of adequate storage. Storage

> Role of Tarpaulin for storing Food Grains

o Tarpaulin is a traditional method of food grains preservation and storage. During the year 2021-2022, the Hon’ble Minister for School Education has made the following Announcement (Announcement No.23) on the floor of Assembly:-

“State Council of Educational Research and Training in collaboration with UNICEF, Chennai will develop life skill training among students of classes 9-12 studying in Government and Government Aided Schools of 44 Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs) in Tamilnadu for the emotional well being and life skills development — Teachers Manual and Students Workbooks based on Art and Games will be developed at a cost of Rs.1.00 crore.”

2. In the letter second read above, the Director, State Council of Educational Research and Training has stated that State Council of Educational Research and Training collaborates with UNICEF in implementing the Programme on Emotional Wellbeing and Life Skills for adolescents studying in the Government and Government Aided High and Higher Secondary Schools in the Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs) of Tamil Nadu. A Teacher’s Manual and a Student’s Workbook will be developed by UNICEF’s Technical Partner, Nalanda Way Foundation. The select SCERT- DIET faculty members review these materials. The reviewed materials will be printed by the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation, Chennai. The Student’s Workbook will be given to each student of the classes 9-12 studying in these schools approximately 2,50,000
